head: claude/mi122-r7-lease-run
title: R7: grade cadence against the same lease RUN, along the right parent
body:
**MI-122.** Tier-1, self-landing (`.github/pr-landing/mi122-r7-lease-run.json` + `.github/pr-automerge-requests/mi122-r7-lease-run.txt`). Session `session_01QRMbr88Ju1XAqsfHxcms5c`, registered as `pending-20260904T224429Z`. Unblocks **#10982**.

## The root

R7 selected a "previous heartbeat" **without establishing that it belonged to the same lease RUN, reached along the right parent**. Two measured instances, one cause.

**(a) A CLAIM over an EXPIRED lease was graded as a late check-in.** `cc984fec` failed at *"746 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat"*. R7's own docstring already exempted a HANDOVER, reasoning that grading one *"would fail the incoming manager for the outgoing one's silence"* — that transfers verbatim to a lease that **died** and was re-claimed, which is a handover to oneself. The holder is unchanged, so the existing exemption could never reach it.

A lease **RUN** is `(holder, claimed_at)`: `manager_lease.py::cmd_claim` stamps a fresh `claimed_at` on every claim and `cmd_heartbeat` preserves it, so the pair names the run and nothing else does. R7 now establishes the run instead of inferring it from the holder alone.

**(b) The previous blob was read from `sha~1`** — the FIRST parent, which on a manager merge into a worker branch is the *worker branch's* stale lease (blocks #10895; `BL-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-R7-MEASURES-CADENCE-ALONG-THE-FIRST-PARENT-...-READS-AS-A-LAPSE`). Every parent is now read and the **latest same-run heartbeat** wins: the manager's silence is wall-clock silence, so the most recent check-in on any line the commit brought together is when it was last heard from.

## What deliberately did NOT change

- **The dead interval is still seen.** What moves is *where* the silence is charged, never *whether* it is reported. A re-claim emits a note naming the interval and the state it was claimed over, and `--self-test` **asserts that note exists** — so a future change that "fixes" R7 by not looking fails the test instead of passing quietly. A silent pass would be worse than the false red.
- **R7's real case still bites.** A manager ALIVE and silent past one TTL still FAILS.
- **No scope exception, no bypass flag.** The operator ruled against a `manager-scope-exception.yaml` entry on 2026-09-04, and none is added. `cmd_claim` returns early on `held_by_me` *without rewriting `claimed_at`*, so a live manager cannot re-claim its way out of a grade; reaching a new run costs either real expiry (reported) or `--force --reason` (recorded in the file). The cheapest way past R7 is still to check in.
- **An absent `claimed_at` still GRADES.** The run cannot be established, and the choice is between dropping enforcement and keeping it. It keeps it and says so. A rule that stops grading whenever a field is missing is one hand-edit from being off — which is the same incentive this unit exists to close.

## Evidence on live history — state the population

**Population: the 46 commits touching `docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json` reachable in a shallow clone of `main` at `--depth=1000`.** Old guard vs new, run over every one:

| | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| R7 FAILs | **3** | **1** |
| verdicts that differ | — | **2 of 46** |

Both changed verdicts are same-holder re-claims **over `state=expired`**, and both still report their dead interval in full:

- `448f086a` "manager state: reclaim the lease…" — **100 minutes** reported
- `2e5ef601` "manager-lease: claim by session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ" (#10670) — **214 minutes** reported

`cb9f0bbb` still FAILS at **131 minutes** — a genuine same-run silence — so the rule's real case is intact.

⚠️ **The live `cc984fec` itself could not be replayed and I am not claiming it was.** It is unreachable from this clone (its branch was squash-merged; the squash `c17b4e7c` on `main` grades as a *handover*, a holder change, so it is not the same shape). The reproduction is in `--self-test`, which produces the identical message and the identical 746-minute figure under mutation.

## Tests — plant + control for both faces, verified by MUTATION

`--self-test` goes **23 → 28 cases**; all 23 pre-existing still pass. Added:

| case | face | asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `8e` PLANT | (a) | re-claim over an expired lease → **clean**, *and* the note names "746 minutes" and `expired` |
| `8f` CONTROL | (a) | the **same 746-minute gap within one run** → still **violation** (R7 only, R6 quiet) |
| `8g` PLANT | (b) | manager merge, stale FIRST parent → **clean** |
| `8h` CONTROL | (b) | merge genuinely 130 min past its **newest** parent → still **violation** |
| `8i` CONTROL | — | no `claimed_at` at all → still **graded** (enforcement kept) |

**Mutation evidence — the fix was removed five ways and each turned exactly one case red:**

| mutation | case that went red | what it printed |
|---|---|---|
| M1 drop the RUN check (same holder ≡ same run) | `8e` | `R7 … -> 746 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat` — **the live message, verbatim** |
| M2 stop reporting the dead interval | `8e` | *"the dead interval must still be REPORTED, not made to disappear"* |
| M3 read only the first parent (`sha~1`) | `8g` | `R7 … -> 140 minutes since this…` on the merge — **the #10895 shape** |
| M4 never grade a merge | `8h` | expected `violation`, got `clean` |
| M5 exempt when `claimed_at` is absent | `8i` | expected `violation`, got `clean` |

M3 leaves `8h` green and M4 leaves `8g` green, so the two faces are independently covered rather than one test carrying both.

## Guards

`python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` after committing: **PASS 59 · FAIL 4 · SKIP 24**.

**All 4 failures are tools absent from this container, not findings, and I am naming them rather than reporting them green:**

- `trainer-capture-watch-guard`, `operator-owed-guard`, `artifact-validity-guard` — all three fail only on their `python3 -m pytest …` step; `python3 -m pytest --version` → **`No module named pytest`**.
- `layer-guard` — `lint-imports` **exit 127**, `command -v lint-imports` → absent.

`artifact-validity-guard`'s **actual check** passes: `check_backlog_refs.py --base origin/main` → *"OK — every tracking id this change introduces resolves to a filed backlog row."* It legitimately caught me first time: I had wrapped the `BL-…` id across two source lines, so the reference resolved to a fragment. The id is now on one line with a comment saying why it must stay there.

**So: I could not run the three pytest guards or the import-layer guard. CI runs them.**

## Adjacent observation, filed not fixed (scope)

**R6 (`supervision_gap`) reads `sha~1` too**, for its "heartbeat not advanced" short-circuit. On a merge with a stale first parent it therefore concludes the heartbeat advanced when it did not, and grades the merge against its own `SESSIONS.json` blob. It did not misfire in any case here and I have **no measured instance**, so I did not touch it — changing a second rule on speculation would also have broken the "a plant that trips two rules proves neither" isolation the R7 tests rely on. Flagging it rather than walking past it.

## Registry

Nothing learned that changes my `SESSIONS.json` row's scope; the manager owns that file and I did not edit it.
